_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-10-26 — the week three Anthropic alias repoints each turned into a price cut, and the week Iris-3B shipped the few-step build this report was waiting for. ONE MISSED FIRING, not three: the last report is dated 2026-10-12 and the schedule is Mondays, so 2026-10-19 did not fire and this is a 14-day gap. NOTHING WAS ADOPTED — no candidate's checkpoint is in config/model-meta.json, no upgrade target is in config/ai-router.yaml, and config/hosts/*.json gained only the project-engine service on 24-10. Three things changed under the previous report and are corrected in the open below: the Open ASR Leaderboard's results datasets now answer 401 to an anonymous fetch, so docs/models.md step 2b no longer works as written; last week's long-form WER figures were averaged over a TedLium split the board removed in May 2026, which flattered every model by about 2.5 WER without changing the ordering; and the Iris-3B entry omitted an 8.88 GB text encoder and called the model unremarkable on B5 when the authors' sampler requires a CUDA GPU. The Open TTS Leaderboard's 19-10 normalizer fix moved every WER on both boards, so every TTS number here is re-read rather than carried.

candidates.why: STILL THE PICK FOR BETENSHI, and the case is now narrower and better evidenced than it read on 12-10. BeTenshi has served stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001 for the 63 days since this entry was raised on 24-08. WHAT THE NEW BUILD CHANGES, stated before the case: the board now drops any row that is missing one of its eleven default datasets instead of averaging it over the subset, which retires last week's whole argument about the `avg` column being a trap — the board fixed it. On that complete-coverage average Cohere is 5.77 and is open #3, not open #2: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B is 5.40 and ibm-granite/granite-speech-5.0-2b, new to the board on 21-10, is 5.68. So this model no longer leads on clean English. IT STILL LEADS ON THE TWO THINGS A MICROPHONE IN A ROOM PRODUCES. On URGENT24 (degraded, noisy speech) it is 9.50 against whisper's 13.73 — a 31% relative error reduction — and it is open #1 there, with only four models ahead of it and all four proprietary APIs (zoom/scribe_v2_pro 7.99, OtterAI/speech-v3.1 8.07, assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro 9.08, elevenlabs/scribe_v2 9.20); the next open model is Qwen3-ASR at 9.93 and granite-speech-5.0-2b at 10.22. On long-form it is 12.23 against whisper's 13.92 and is open #1, the seven models above it all proprietary, the next open model 0.95 WER behind (thewhisper-large-v3-turbo 13.18). 902 RTFx against whisper's 470, for a 4.13 GB download. ONE BOARD NOW READS IT AS UNMEASURED and the report should say so rather than quote the old number: the multilingual board's headline average covers seven languages including Hindi, Cohere has no Hindi score, so it is UNRANKED there at 6/7 coverage. On the six European languages it and whisper both have, it is 3.84 against whisper's 4.57 (de 3.10/4.00, fr 4.02/6.24, it 2.97/4.45, es 2.81/3.35, pt 5.99/4.94, nl 4.17/4.42) — better on five of six, and second among open models to thewhisper-large-v3-turbo's 3.61, which is held out for the reasons in notes. Its 14 declared languages include ARABIC, which this box has an evaluation harness for (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md) and which no other candidate here covers. UNREMARKABLE ON B5, which moved its stt to an 8-bit MLX Qwen3-ASR build on 20-09 and has the pool for anything on this list. The caveat is unchanged and is a click-through, not an application: `gated: auto` under apache-2.0, so a human accepts the terms once. 101,814 downloads in the last 30 days (129,680 a fortnight ago) and 3,492,438 all-time.

candidates.why: THE ENTRY THE NEW BUILD VINDICATES. On 12-10 this report argued that Qwen3-ASR's posted average of 5.75 understated it, that three models reading above it (Phi-4-multimodal 5.02, granite-speech-3.3-8b 5.26 and -3.3-2b 5.36) had no URGENT2024 score, and that on the datasets all four shared it led them. The 21-10 board now drops incomplete rows from the ranked table instead of averaging them over a subset, and with that fixed Qwen3-ASR is OPEN #1 ON ENGLISH SHORT-FORM outright at 5.40, rank 9 of 57 overall and ahead of every open model including granite-speech-5.0-2b (5.68) and Cohere (5.77); the eight rows above it are all proprietary APIs. Phi-4 and the granite-3.3 pair are now off the ranked table entirely. 819 RTFx against whisper-large-v3's 470, and whisper is 7.16 at rank 39. THIS SPEAKS ONLY TO BETENSHI: it has been in service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit`, and BeTenshi's :8001 is still whisper-large-v3. WHERE IT LOSES, unchanged and still decisive for the general route: multilingual 6.56 against whisper's 8.18 on the seven-language average, but 5.52 against whisper's 4.57 on the six European languages both measure — worse than the model it would replace on four of the six despite 30 advertised; ABSENT from the long-form board, so nothing is known about a meeting recording; and 9.93 on URGENT24, second-best open model but 0.43 behind Cohere. So Cohere remains the general pick and this is the narrow one: take it on BeTenshi only if that box transcribes short English utterances and nothing else, which is what voice input in the Studio is. Five weeks in service on B5 is evidence it runs, not evidence it is right for the other box. 341,248 downloads in the last 30 days, 929,168 all-time.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 26-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo; repo lastModified still 2026-09-09. HF publishes NO parameter count for either AuK repo and the safetensors index carries no dtype summary, so estimateFromParams() must not be used on them — the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.4 bytes/param, so that figure describes one component. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. Benchmarks are the Open TTS Leaderboard build dated 21-10-2026 (hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results at rev 0a9c3bcd4035b26e0d74d3a64810008a2f811bb9, read through the Space's own _refresh_leaderboard endpoint because the results dataset still returns 401 to an anonymous fetch). EVERY NUMBER HERE IS RE-READ, NOT CARRIED: the board's 19-10 build was a text-normalizer fix — 'keep content within parentheses/brackets' — which moved WER for every model on both boards.

candidates.why: STILL THE SECOND CLONING VOICE, and the normalizer fix made the margin over the running service BIGGER while costing it its rank. On CV3-Eval English in cloning mode — the one dataset and language where this model and the service on :8004 are both scored — AuK-Flash is 2.30 WER / 72.67 SIM / 26.61 RTFx against ChatterboxMultilingualTTS's 3.42 / 53.13 / 0.99. Both WERs fell with the 19-10 fix (from 3.35 and 4.43), and the gap widened from 24% to 33% lower word error; SIM and RTFx are identical to three decimals, so +19.54 speaker-similarity points on the one axis a cloning service exists for, and 27x the throughput, under the same MIT licence. local-chatterbox IS the Multilingual variant per config/model-meta.json, so that is the right comparison and not the English-only ChatterboxTTS sibling. WHAT GOT WORSE IS ITS STANDING, not its output, and the honest reading is that WER is no longer its argument: it is now 10th of 19 on the English cloning board behind k2-fsa/OmniVoice 1.38 (cc-by-nc), bosonai/higgs-tts-3-4b 1.40 (custom), fishaudio/s2-pro 1.48 (custom), OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS 1.74 (apache-2.0), Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base 1.80 (apache-2.0), kyutai/pocket-tts 1.86 and Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 RL 1.94. SIM IS WHERE IT STILL WINS, and it wins it outright among clean licences: AuK 73.00 and AuK-Flash 72.67 are the top two SIM scores on the whole board, ahead of OmniVoice 70.05 (non-commercial), openbmb/VoxCPM2 69.02 (apache-2.0) and Qwen3-TTS-Base 66.96. Take Flash and not the base: same 6.76 GB, 0.14 WER worse, 6x the speed. THE NEW METRIC IS NOT KIND and the report should say so: the 21-10 build added UTMOS, a predicted naturalness MOS, and AuK-Flash scores 3.60 — bottom of the cloning board, against Qwen3-TTS-Base 3.93 and Kokoro's 4.51 on the reading board. Chatterbox has no UTMOS score, so this is NOT a comparison with the running service; it is a reason to listen to output before committing the service. THE COST, unchanged: AuK-Flash declares zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 including Arabic, and neither board measures Arabic at all. So this is an ADDITION for English and Chinese, not a repoint of :8004 — and a new service to write, because AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro's 0.4 GB and Chatterbox's measured 3.0 GB without disturbing either; unremarkable on B5. ADOPTION IS NOT JUST THIN, IT IS FALLING, and that is a fact against it: 1,073 downloads in the last 30 days against 2,963 a fortnight ago, 3,991 all-time.

candidates.why: THE NON-ENGLISH READING VOICE FOR BETENSHI, and after the normalizer fix it is the best CLEAN-LICENSED model on the nine-language board. In service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice`, so this speaks only to BeTenshi. DO NOT REPOINT :8002 AT IT: on the English no-cloning board Kokoro-82M is 1.10 average WER at 68.03 RTFx with UTMOS 4.51, against this model's 1.41 at 13.20 and UTMOS 4.43 — both moved with the fix (from 1.46 and 1.71), the ordering did not, and for reading English aloud the 82M model already installed is faster, more intelligible and a fortieth of the size. WHAT SURVIVES IS BREADTH, and it is a real gap. Across all nine languages CV3-Eval measures, this model ranks 4th at 3.64 average WER — one place lower than on 12-10, not because it got worse but because fishaudio/s2-pro (3.23) and fishaudio/drama-3 (3.46) entered above it, and both are `custom` licence, as is nothing else between them; k2-fsa/OmniVoice leads at 2.80 and is cc-by-nc. So among models whose terms are already known it is #1, ahead of MOSS-TTS 3.78 and VoxCPM2 4.47. Kokoro is unranked because it has no German, Korean or Russian at all, and Chatterbox — the multilingual voice this box gained on 18-09 — ranks 11th at 10.70. Per language, reading without cloning: German 5.08 against Chatterbox's 16.43, French 4.68 against 14.93, Russian 5.18 against 13.04, Japanese 5.90 against 8.82, Korean 4.24 against 8.14. So if BeTenshi needs to read non-English text aloud this is the model, and it beats what shipped on 18-09 by two to three times on error. B5 has already made that call for itself. The correction from 21-09 stands and is re-confirmed on this build: the board records CustomVoice as NOT supporting voice cloning — 'CustomVoice' is a speaker bank. The `-Base` sibling is the cloner and is now 5th on the CV3 English cloning board at 1.80 WER / 66.96 SIM, which makes it the strongest apache-2.0 cloner measured and worth a line beside AuK-Flash above: 13.6 SIM points lower, 0.50 WER better, and ten declared languages against AuK's two. Downloads by metric, as docs/models.md requires: 1,914,864 in the last 30 days, 17,513,403 all-time.

candidates.why: CARRIED FOR A SEVENTH WEEK, AND THIS IS THE LAST ONE IT GETS WITHOUT EVIDENCE. First raised 2026-09-07, dated from git. It is STILL ABSENT FROM ALL FOUR BOARDS on the 21-10 build, so after seven weeks and four board builds its accuracy remains unmeasured, and its 30-day downloads have fallen 68% — 1,943 against 6,106 a fortnight ago, 13,605 all-time. The doubt raised on 12-10 is unchanged and still the sharpest thing known about the family: the one measured member, microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF, is 19.50 on URGENT24 against whisper's 13.73 and Cohere's 9.50 while sitting at 8.16 on the full English average — the worst noise score of any model in its WER band, and noise is precisely what a live microphone delivers. SO SET A STOP RULE rather than re-listing this indefinitely: if the next board build still does not measure this checkpoint, drop the entry and keep only the diarisation alternative below. WHAT STILL STANDS, and it is why it is not dropped today: it is the only MIT-licensed model on this list that streams speaker-attributed transcription as audio arrives, and local-whisper on BeTenshi cannot show live text or tell two speakers apart at all. So: if STREAMING is the actual requirement, install it behind its own service and do not repoint the stt capability at it — the general route belongs to Cohere. If DIARISATION ALONE is the need, take OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize instead: it is measured (6.17 English average, 12.74 URGENT24, absent from long-form, 6/7 multilingual coverage), it is 0.91 GB against 5.65, and it is Apache-2.0 — better on every axis except the streaming itself. On BeTenshi 5.65 GB sits comfortably beside the speech services; the 7B sibling at 17.36 GB runs alone there and blocks every image model, and is unremarkable on B5, which is where the 7B goes if its accuracy is ever wanted.

candidates.name: Iris-3B Turbo (4-step pixel-space diffusion, + depth and upscaler heads)
candidates.params: 2.99B (turbo/ is a bf16 export of all 3B; the repo root is the same model at fp32)

requirement.basis: THIS REQUIREMENT IS A CORRECTION OF THE 12-10 ENTRY, in two ways, and both numbers moved. FIRST, the checkpoint recommended is now turbo/, not the repo root: turbo/model.safetensors is 5,975,089,200 B, read 26-10, which is 2.0000 bytes per the repo's 2,987,511,888 params and the card confirms 'the stage-2 EMA weights, exported in bf16'. The root model.safetensors is still 11,950,112,680 B at fp32. SECOND, the 12-10 entry's 13.7 GB VRAM omitted the TEXT ENCODER entirely: the card says Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct 'downloads automatically on the first run', and that repo is 8,875,719,344 B of weights (4.44B params, BF16) and 8,887,292,732 B whole. So disk is 5,975,089,200 + 8,887,292,732 = 14,862,381,932 B, and the resident weight set for one generation is 5,975,089,200 + 8,875,719,344 = 14,850,808,544 B, x 1.15 runtime overhead = 17.1 GB. NOT MEASURED and NOT A PEAK: activation cost at one megapixel is unknown and pixel-space models carry more of it than latent ones. A pipeline that frees the encoder after prompt encoding would cut the resident figure to about 6.9 GB, but the authors' sample.py loads both, so the honest number is both. The depth/ and upscaler/ folders are 11,952,738,184 and 11,950,112,680 B and are NOT in this figure — add about 12 GB each if those heads are wanted; the whole repo is now 41.91 GB across 34 files. Use the card's own exclude list: `hf download speridlabs/iris-3b --include "turbo/*"`.

candidates.why: THE FIND OF THE WEEK, AND IT IS AN UPDATE TO LAST WEEK'S ENTRY RATHER THAN A NEW MODEL: the repo gained a `turbo/` folder on 2026-10-12, hours after the 12-10 read, and it answers both costs that entry flagged as unmeasured. Turbo is a 4-STEP distillation of all 3B parameters (TDM, full fine-tune, not a LoRA) with CFG baked into the weights, against the base model's default of CFG 3 at 100 STEPS — the authors quote a 1024x1024 image in about 0.7 s on one H100 at batch 4 — and it ships at 5.98 GB bf16 where the base is 11.95 GB fp32, which is the bf16 build the 12-10 entry said did not exist. AND IT IS NOT A QUALITY SACRIFICE, on the authors' own numbers under the official scorers: GenEval 0.820 against the base's 0.798, DPG-Bench 86.68 against 86.52, and behind the base on long rendered text (LongText-Bench EN 0.804 vs 0.857) and on OneIG-Bench EN (0.516 vs 0.540, the gap mostly text and diversity). STATE WHAT THOSE NUMBERS ARE NOT: they are the authors' own, there is still no third-party image-generation board, and nothing installed on either box has been scored on the same harness here, so this is NOT a head-to-head against Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.2-klein-4B or HiDream-O1 — it is the first candidate in this lane with any published number at all. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE 12-10 ENTRY, both material. (1) It said Iris-3B 'beats local-flux-schnell, which is still in config/model-meta.json'. It is not: local-flux-schnell was removed from model-meta.json by commit cdce268 on 2026-10-03, which reached main in the 14-10 merge, so that comparison is gone and with it the entry's footprint argument. What is left is a CAPABILITY argument, which is the stronger one anyway: the same pixel-space prior, fine-tuned without architectural change, ships monocular DEPTH ESTIMATION (AbsRel 0.071, delta-1 0.946, zero-shot mean of NYUv2/KITTI/ETH3D/ScanNet/DIODE under the Marigold V2 protocol) and 4x RESTORATION/UPSCALING (LPIPS 0.292, PSNR 20.68 on DIV2K validation) in the same repo, both run with the empty prompt and no text encoder. Nothing on BeTenshi or B5 does depth or super-resolution at all. (2) It called the model 'unremarkable in B5's pool'. THAT WAS WRONG AND THE REASON IS NOT SIZE: the card's Get started section says 'You need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA', so on B5 the 128 GB pool is not the binding constraint, the code path is — the same shape of refusal as Edge0-35B-A3B in reverse. No `runtimes` pin is set, because the weights are plain safetensors and portable in format; it is the authors' sampler that is CUDA-only, and docs/models.md says runtimes must speak only where the FORMAT pins the hardware. SO THIS IS A BETENSHI EVALUATE: apache-2.0, not gated, 14.86 GB of disk for the turbo model plus its encoder, 17.1 GB resident on a 31.8 GB card — which collides with the 20 GB Qwen-Image service if that is up and fits beside the speech stack if it is not. Still only 1,671 all-time downloads, three weeks old, and nobody has A/B'd it against anything installed. Worth the download to find out whether the depth and upscaler heads earn their place; it is the only thing on this list that adds a capability rather than replacing one. A community 460 MB rank-64 LoRA exists (pentacoxian-dev/iris-3b-turbo-lora) and scores below the official turbo on every metric (GenEval 0.760), so take the 6 GB checkpoint.

upgrades.why: THE ONE TO DO FIRST, and it changed in three ways in the fourteen days since it was raised on 2026-10-12 (dated from git, not incremented). (1) THE AVAILABILITY FLOOR HAS LAPSED. Anthropic's deprecation page gave claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 a retirement commitment of 'Not sooner than October 15, 2026'. That date has passed, the commitment was NOT extended, and the row still reads exactly that. It is the only model this router fronts whose guaranteed-availability floor is in the past. (2) IT IS NOW LEGACY. The models overview page lists it under 'Legacy models (still available)', which Anthropic defines as 'will no longer receive updates and might be deprecated in the future' — on 12-10 this entry said the model was listed ACTIVE, and on the deprecation table it still is, so the two pages now disagree and the overview is the newer signal. SAY WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN, because the gpt-5.5 entry already got burned on exactly this: the model is NOT deprecated, no retirement date is assigned, and Anthropic promises at least 60 days' notice before retiring a publicly released model, so nothing breaks tomorrow. What is gone is the floor. (3) AND THE NEW ARGUMENT IS PRICE, which this entry did not have a fortnight ago: Anthropic's pricing page, read 26-10, gives claude-haiku-4-5 $1.00 / $5.00 per 1M input/output tokens and claude-haiku-5-5 $0.10 / $0.50 for prompts up to 100,000 tokens — A TEN-FOLD CUT on both sides of the meter — rising to $0.50 / $2.50 above 100k, still half the old price. claude-haiku-5-5 is Active with a floor of October 7, 2027, and a 1M context against haiku-4-5's 200k. PREREQUISITE, and it is shared with the next four entries: claude-haiku-5-5 is NOT in ai-router.yaml. The last wire-all ran 2026-09-18 and this model shipped around 2026-10-07, so discovery has not swept since. Run the console's Wire all first, then edit the alias — one click and one restart, then one line by hand.

OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT and MOSS-Image-Base landed 11-10, are the top trending text-to-image repos on the hub, and are APACHE-2.0 AND NOT GATED — which on licence alone makes them the most interesting image release since Z-Image. A week of community work has already grown around them (GGUF repacks, an FP16-fixed build, a 4-step adapter LoRA, colour/depth control adapters), which is a better adoption signal than likes. THE FOOTPRINT IS WHAT REFUSES THEM, and it is the familiar shape: HF reports 5.08B params, and the repo is 27,229,060,886 B — the transformer is three shards summing 10,164,664,216 B (= 2 bytes x 5.08B, so that count describes the transformer only), the TEXT ENCODER is four shards summing 16,785,478,992 B, and the VAE 249,521,372 B. So 27.23 GB of weights for a '5.08B' model. On BETENSHI that is 31.3 GB at 1.15 overhead against a 31.8 GB card, which is the local-flux-schnell situation exactly — admission control rejected schnell at a measured 31.72 GiB — so it would at best run alone and at worst not at all, and the few-step community builds have not been measured by anyone. On B5 the 128 GB pool swallows it without comment and `library_name: diffusers` means the stack exists there, which makes this the rare image model that is a B5 question rather than a BeTenshi one.
